```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Kim et al. (2024) gave a long-acting intramuscular niclosamide formulation to
Golden Syrian hamsters and modelled plasma and lung-tissue concentrations
jointly. They fitted two models that differ only in how drug exchanges between
plasma and a perfusion-limited lung compartment:

* `Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster` -- the final **power-law** model (Table 2,
  Equation 2), `dAlung/dt = Qlung * (Cplasma^Xcl - Clung)`.
* `Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster_linear` -- the **linear partition-coefficient**
  alternative (Appendix S1 Table S3, Equation 1),
  `dAlung/dt = Qlung * (Cplasma - Clung / Kp)`.

The power-law model was preferred (OFV -256.33 versus -200.84, and a better
lung VPC) and was used for the dose optimisation.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster"))$reference`
* Description (power law): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster"))$description`
* Description (linear): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster_linear"))$description`
* Article: [Clin Transl Sci 2024;17:e13833](https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13833)

# Population

Twenty-five 7-week-old male Golden Syrian hamsters (SLC Japan) received a
single intramuscular injection after a 7-day acclimatisation. Plasma
pharmacokinetics were measured at 55, 96, 128 and 240 mg/kg (n = 5 per dose),
and lung tissue was collected from a separate group dosed at 240 mg/kg, with
sampling at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 48, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504 and 672 h
(Methods, Study design). Body weights are not reported. The model was fitted in
NONMEM 7.5.1 with FOCE-I on log-transformed observations.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Power law (Table 2) | Linear (Table S3) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, L/h) | 0.485 | 0.49 | |
| `lvc` (Vc, L) | 0.371 | 0.35 | |
| `lq` (Q inter, L/h) | 0.365 | 0.34 | |
| `lvp` (Vp, L) | 1.647 | 1.58 | |
| `lq_lung` (Q lung, L/h) | 0.0613, not estimated | 0.0613, not estimated | allometric interpolation |
| `lv_lung` (V l, L) | 0.000919, not estimated | 0.000919, not estimated | allometric interpolation |
| `lpow_lung` (X cl) | 0.753 | -- | Equation 2 |
| `lkp_lung` (Kp) | -- | 0.27 | Equation 1 |
| `lka` (K A1, 1/h) | 0.042 | 0.04 | fast depot |
| `lkamax` (K A2, 1/h) | 0.002 | 0.002 | Table S3 prints 0.00; bootstrap median 0.002 used |
| `lra` (1 / Lambda, 1/h) | 1 / 155.80 | 1 / 164.60 | Weibull time scale |
| `lgam1` (Gamma) | 7.199 | 22.08 | Weibull shape |
| `lfdepot2` (F) | 0.430 | 0.42 | fraction to slow depot |
| `etalvc` | 0.299 | 0.53 | omega^2 |
| `etalcl` | 0.0233 | 0.16 | omega^2 |
| `etalfdepot2` | 0.169 | 0.33 | omega^2 |
| `expSd` (plasma) | 0.373 | 0.39 | log-scale SD |
| `expSd_Clung` (lung) | 0.361 | 0.50 | log-scale SD |
| Absorption | Figure 1 | Figure 1 | fast depot `1 - F` at Ka1; slow depot `F` at `Ka2 * WB`, `WB = 1 - exp(-(time/lambda)^gamma)` |
| Lung exchange | Equation 2 | Equation 1 | |

# Virtual cohort

The doses are in mg/kg and the model volumes and clearances are absolute (L,
L/h), so a body weight is needed to turn a mg/kg dose into an amount. The paper
does not report one. The maintainers used **0.12 kg** for every animal: with
complete absorption, dose = CL x AUCinf, and Table 1 AUCinf with the model's CL
of 0.485 L/h implies 0.12, 0.10, 0.12 and 0.17 kg at 55, 96, 128 and
240 mg/kg, consistent with the usual weight of an 8-week-old male Golden Syrian
hamster.

```{r cohort}
body_wt <- 0.12 # kg, assumed (see above)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 48, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504, 672,
  seq(4, 672, by = 4)
)))

# One intramuscular dose is two dose records with the full amount (depot and
# depot2); the model's f() splits the dose between the fast and slow depots.
make_cohort <- function(n, dose_mgkg, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  amt <- dose_mgkg * body_wt
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, cmt = c("depot", "depot2")) |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = amt)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(cmt = "Cc", evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(dose_group = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg")) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

dose_levels <- c(55, 96, 128, 240)
n_per_group <- 100L
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(dose_levels), function(i) {
  make_cohort(n_per_group, dose_levels[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_group)
}))
events$dose_group <- factor(events$dose_group, levels = paste(dose_levels, "mg/kg"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "cmt")])))
```

Observation rows name the endpoint `Cc`: both models declare two endpoints
(`Cc` and `Clung`), and the lung concentration is returned as a column on every
row.

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod_pow <- readModelDb("Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster")
mod_lin <- readModelDb("Kim_2024_niclosamide_hamster_linear")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240530)
sim_pow <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pow, events = events, keep = "dose_group") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(model = "Power")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240530)
sim_lin <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_lin, events = events, keep = "dose_group") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(model = "Linear")
sim <- bind_rows(sim_pow, sim_lin)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim$Cc)), all(is.finite(sim$Clung)))
```

Typical-value (no between-animal variability) predictions are used for the
structural checks and the NCA comparison:

```{r simulate-typical}
typ <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pow), events = events |> filter(id %% n_per_group == 1L),
                  keep = "dose_group") |> as.data.frame() |> mutate(model = "Power"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_lin), events = events |> filter(id %% n_per_group == 1L),
                  keep = "dose_group") |> as.data.frame() |> mutate(model = "Linear")
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2 -- plasma and lung concentration-time profiles

Figure 2 of Kim 2024 is a prediction-corrected VPC pooled across dose groups,
on the natural-log scale. The panels below show the simulated 5th, 50th and
95th percentiles (between-animal variability only) of the plasma concentration
by dose group and of the lung concentration in the 240 mg/kg group, for both
models.

```{r figure-2-plasma, fig.height = 5}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(model, dose_group, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, log(Q50), colour = model, fill = model)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = log(Q05), ymax = log(Q95)), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose_group) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "log plasma concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Plasma panels of Figure 2 of Kim 2024 (simulated, 100 animals per dose)."
  )
```

```{r figure-2-lung}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 504, dose_group == "240 mg/kg") |>
  group_by(model, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Clung, 0.05), Q50 = median(Clung), Q95 = quantile(Clung, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, log(Q50), colour = model, fill = model)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = log(Q05), ymax = log(Q95)), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "log lung concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Lung panels of Figure 2 of Kim 2024 (simulated, 240 mg/kg)."
  )
```

As in Figure 2, both models show a fast-absorption peak in the first day, a
trough near 96 h and a second, flatter peak once the Weibull-triggered slow
depot switches on (lambda = 156-165 h). The paper's observed plasma median is
about 5.7 log units at the peak, 2.6 at 96 h and 3.0 at 250-330 h; the observed
lung median is about 5.3 at the peak, 3.0 at 96 h and 2.6-3.2 thereafter.

## Plasma-lung relationship: power law versus partition coefficient

The two models differ in the lung-to-plasma concentration ratio. With a lung
volume of 0.92 mL and a blood flow of 61 mL/h the lung equilibrates within
minutes, so the lung concentration tracks its equilibrium value,
`Cplasma^0.753` (power) or `0.27 * Cplasma` (linear). The check below confirms
that the typical-value solution sits on that relationship once the absorption
peak has passed.

```{r lung-equilibrium}
eq_chk <- typ |>
  filter(time >= 48, dose_group == "240 mg/kg") |>
  mutate(
    Clung_eq = ifelse(model == "Power", Cc^0.753, 0.27 * Cc),
    rel = Clung / Clung_eq - 1
  )
eq_chk |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(max_abs_rel_dev_pct = 100 * max(abs(rel)), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Deviation of the simulated lung concentration from its equilibrium value, 48-672 h.")
stopifnot(max(abs(eq_chk$rel)) < 0.02)

typ |>
  filter(time > 0, dose_group == "240 mg/kg") |>
  ggplot(aes(Cc, Clung, colour = model)) +
  geom_path() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Lung concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical animal, 240 mg/kg. The power law is a straight line of slope 0.753 on log-log axes."
  )
```

The amount of drug in the lung is negligible against the dose (well under
0.01%), so including the lung exchange in the central mass balance does not
change the plasma profile.

```{r lung-mass}
typ |>
  filter(model == "Power", dose_group == "240 mg/kg") |>
  summarise(max_lung_fraction_of_dose = max(lung) / (240 * body_wt)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 8)
```

# PKNCA validation

Plasma NCA by dose group over the sampling window (0-672 h), and lung NCA in
the 240 mg/kg group over 0-504 h (the extent of the lung panels of Figure 2),
on the simulated individual concentrations at the paper's nominal sampling
times.

```{r pknca}
nominal <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 48, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504, 672)

run_nca <- function(df, conc_col, end_time) {
  conc_df <- df |>
    filter(time %in% nominal, time <= end_time) |>
    mutate(conc = .data[[conc_col]]) |>
    filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
    select(id, time, conc, dose_group)
  conc_df <- bind_rows(
    conc_df,
    conc_df |> distinct(id, dose_group) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)
  ) |>
    distinct(id, dose_group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, dose_group, time)
  # Each dose record carries the full amount (f() splits it), so the depot
  # record alone is the administered dose.
  dose_df <- events |>
    filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot", id %in% conc_df$id) |>
    select(id, time, amt, dose_group)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | dose_group + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | dose_group + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = c(0, 0), end = c(end_time, Inf),
    cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
    half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE), aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE)
  )
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

nca_plasma_pow <- run_nca(sim_pow, "Cc", 672)
nca_lung_pow <- run_nca(sim_pow |> filter(dose_group == "240 mg/kg"), "Clung", 504)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 1 of Kim 2024 reports means of five animals per group.

```{r nca-compare}
published_plasma <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_group, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~half.life, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs,
  "55 mg/kg", 160, 7.8, 283, 10938, 13684,
  "96 mg/kg", 225, 12.0, 240, 16845, 19266,
  "128 mg/kg", 431, 4.4, 332, 26278, 32779,
  "240 mg/kg", 2086, 7.3, 351, 68494, 84064
)
published_lung <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_group, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~half.life, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs,
  "240 mg/kg", 256, 11.6, 226, 16377, 21821
)
nca_units <- c(
  cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", half.life = "h",
  auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"
)

knitr::kable(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = nca_plasma_pow, reference = published_plasma,
    by = "dose_group", units = nca_units, tolerance_pct = 20
  ),
  caption = "Plasma, power-law model: simulated (median) vs. Table 1 (mean). * differs by >20%."
)
knitr::kable(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = nca_lung_pow, reference = published_lung,
    by = "dose_group", units = nca_units, tolerance_pct = 20
  ),
  caption = "Lung, power-law model, 240 mg/kg: simulated (median) vs. Table 1 (mean). * differs by >20%."
)
```

Plasma AUC agrees with Table 1 within about 20% at 55, 96 and 128 mg/kg, and
lung AUCinf at 240 mg/kg within a few percent. The starred rows have known
causes. Table 1 is more than dose-proportional at 240 mg/kg (Cmax 2086 ng/mL,
4.8-fold the 128 mg/kg group for 1.9-fold the dose), which the
linear-clearance model cannot reproduce, so the 240 mg/kg plasma Cmax and AUC
are low; the lung Cmax is low for the same reason. Simulated Cmax is 28-52%
high at 55 and 96 mg/kg, and Tmax in the five-animal groups is highly variable
(SD 2-11 h). The assumed 0.12 kg body weight scales every simulated
concentration. NCA half-lives depend on whether the last points fall on the
secondary peak (lung NCA stops at 504 h, mid-way down the slow phase), so they
are reported for completeness only.

```{r nca-structural-gate}
# Typical-value plasma AUC over 0-672 h against Table 1 at the three doses where
# the data are dose-proportional. A mis-transcribed clearance, volume or unit
# moves this by far more than the 30% allowed for the unreported body weight.
typ_auc <- typ |>
  filter(model == "Power", time %in% nominal) |>
  group_by(dose_group) |>
  summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(dose_group = as.character(dose_group)) |>
  inner_join(published_plasma |> select(dose_group, auclast), by = "dose_group") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc / auclast - 1))
knitr::kable(typ_auc, digits = 1, caption = "Typical-animal plasma AUC0-672 vs. Table 1 AUClast.")
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_auc$pct_diff[typ_auc$dose_group != "240 mg/kg"]) < 30))
```

# Dose optimisation (Figure 3)

The authors searched for the intramuscular dose at which more than 90% of
simulated hamsters keep the lung concentration above the in vitro IC50 against
SARS-CoV-2 (0.28 uM) for as long as possible. With a niclosamide molar mass of
327.12 g/mol the IC50 is 91.6 ng/mL, matching the dashed line of Figure 3a. The
paper reports a minimum dose of about 1115 mg/kg, giving a maximum duration of
72 h, and no dose up to 1500 mg/kg reaching 168 h.

The grid below uses 100 animals per dose at 100 mg/kg steps (the paper used
5 mg/kg steps) and counts the time from the dose until the individual lung
concentration first falls back below the IC50, without residual error.

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 3.5}
ic50 <- 0.28 * 327.12 # ng/mL
opt_doses <- seq(300, 1500, by = 100)
opt_times <- seq(0, 168, by = 1)
opt_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(opt_doses), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1L) * 100L + seq_len(100L)
  amt <- opt_doses[i] * body_wt
  bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, cmt = c("depot", "depot2")) |>
      mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = amt),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = opt_times) |>
      mutate(cmt = "Cc", evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(dose = opt_doses[i])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240531)
opt_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pow, events = opt_events, keep = "dose") |>
  as.data.frame()

dur <- opt_sim |>
  group_by(id, dose) |>
  summarise(
    t_below = {
      below <- time > 0 & Clung < ic50
      if (any(below)) min(time[below]) else Inf
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

success <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = opt_doses, duration = c(24, 48, 72, 96, 120)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(ratio = 100 * mean(dur$t_below[dur$dose == dose] >= duration)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(success, aes(dose, factor(duration), fill = ratio)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey60") +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#2d1e3e", "#3fa9f5", "#7cf07c", "#ff9900", "#8b0000"), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (mg/kg)", y = "Duration (h)", fill = "Success (%)",
    caption = "Figure 3b of Kim 2024: share of animals with lung concentration above the IC50 for each duration."
  )

success |>
  filter(duration == 72) |>
  rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Animals above IC50 for 72 h (%)" = ratio) |>
  select(-duration) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0)
```

The simulated grid reproduces the shape of Figure 3b: 24 and 48 h are covered
in more than 90% of animals from moderate doses, 72 h coverage rises steeply
with dose, and 96-120 h is essentially never reached. The 72 h crossing is
later than the paper's: at 1100 mg/kg about half the simulated animals stay
above the IC50 for 72 h (the median duration is close to 72 h), and 90% is not
reached by 1500 mg/kg. This is recorded as a known deviation rather than
tuned. The dose needed for a given lung concentration scales with the
unreported body weight, and the paper's success criterion and its inclusion of
residual error are only partly described. Figure 3b also shows some success at
96-120 h for the highest doses, which a contiguous-duration criterion without
residual error cannot produce.

```{r figure-3-gate}
# Trend only (see the deviation above): 72 h coverage is low at 600 mg/kg and
# high at 1500 mg/kg. Realised 2% and 78% at 16 threads with 100 animals per dose.
r72 <- success |> filter(duration == 72)
stopifnot(
  r72$ratio[r72$dose == 600] < 30,
  r72$ratio[r72$dose == 1500] > 50
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Body weight.** Not reported. A uniform 0.12 kg was used to convert mg/kg
  doses to amounts, chosen from the weights implied by Table 1 AUCinf and the
  model clearance (0.10-0.17 kg) and consistent with 8-week-old male Golden
  Syrian hamsters. Every simulated concentration scales with it.
- **Concentration units of the power law.** The power law is not
  unit-invariant. Figure 2 plots log concentrations in ng/mL for both plasma
  and lung, and the observed lung Cmax at 240 mg/kg (256 ng/mL) is close to the
  observed plasma Cmax raised to 0.753 (2086^0.753 = 316), so the model uses
  plasma and lung concentrations in ng/mL. Dosing is in mg and volumes in L,
  with the factor of 1000 written into `model()`.
- **Central-lung mass balance.** Equations 1 and 2 give only the lung
  equation. Figure 1 draws a two-way arrow between central and lung, so the
  same flux is subtracted from central. Because the lung holds well under
  0.01% of the dose, this choice has no visible effect on plasma.
- **Weibull switch time.** Figure 1 writes the Weibull function of `time`; the
  model uses time since the start of the simulation (`t`), which equals time
  after the dose for the single-dose design of the study. For repeated dosing
  the switch would need to be re-expressed per dose.
- **Variability scale.** Table 2 does not say whether the IIV values are
  variances or standard deviations. They are read as omega^2 (the usual NONMEM
  report). The residual values are read as log-scale standard deviations: the
  observed 5th-95th percentile spread in the plasma panels of Figure 2 is about
  1 log unit late in the profile, which a variance of 0.373 (SD 0.61, spread at
  least 2 log units) could not produce.
- **IIV on F.** The paper investigated additive and exponential IIV without
  naming the final form; exponential IIV is used. Under it the slow-depot
  fraction exceeds 1 in about 2% (power law) and 7% (linear) of simulated
  animals, which would give the fast depot a negative dose. The fraction is
  capped at 1 in `model()`.
- **Linear model (Table S3).** Values are printed to two decimals. K A2 is
  printed as 0.00; the bootstrap median 0.002 (5th-95th 0.001-0.002) from the
  same table is used, which also equals the power-law estimate. The Table S3
  bootstrap medians of the IIV rows (0.023, 0.1085, 0.269) do not match the
  final estimates (0.53, 0.16, 0.33); the final estimates are used.
- **IC50 conversion.** The molar mass of niclosamide (327.12 g/mol) is not
  given in the paper; it converts the 0.28 uM IC50 to 91.6 ng/mL.
- **Dose-optimisation replication.** The paper's success criterion, dose step
  (5 mg/kg) and inclusion of residual error are only partly described; the grid
  above uses 100 mg/kg steps, no residual error, and the time until the lung
  concentration first falls below the IC50. The simulated 72 h crossing is
  above 1500 mg/kg rather than at 1115 mg/kg (see Figure 3 above).
- **Numerical floor in the power law.** The power-law model raises
  `max(Cc, 0)` to the power 0.753: an animal whose whole dose is in the slow
  depot has plasma near zero for days, and a non-integer power of a tiny
  negative integrator undershoot is NaN.
- No erratum or correction notice for Kim 2024 was found as of 2026-10-30.
